children: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo has stated that Nigeria is committed to deepening bilateral ties with India in such a way that the partnership will not only strengthen the country’s aviation infrastructure but also create opportunities for Nigerian professionals to acquire the skills and exposure needed to compete globally
The minister gave the hint when, Received in audience the Indian High Commissioner to Nigeria, His Excellency, Abhishek Singh at the Ministry’s headquarters in Abuja.

Keyamo thanked the High Commissioner for the visit and welcomed his proposals, noting that India’s record in aviation, particularly in the area of capacity building, offers valuable lessons for Nigeria as the Ministry pursues the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu, in the aviation and aerospace sector.

He stated that the ministry is committed to deepening bilateral ties that will not only strengthen the country’s aviation infrastructure, but also create opportunities for Nigerian professionals to acquire the skills and exposure needed to compete globally.

The minister identified training, capacity building and the transfer of knowledge as priority areas for the ministry, noting that the partnership with India should be structured in a way that equips Nigerian engineers, pilots, air traffic controllers and other aviation professionals with the expertise required to drive the sector forward.
The minister directed that a technical team be set up to work out the details of the proposed partnership between both countries.

Speaking during the visit, the Indian High Commissioner said Nigeria’s airports are performing very well, adding that each visit reinforces his conviction that both countries have much to gain from each other.
He stated that there is tremendous potential in the industry and that he sees at least six or seven areas in which both countries can collaborate.

The High Commissioner expressed his desire for the Minister to visit India, adding that the Indian Minister for Civil Aviation, whom he described as a very young and dynamic man, would also want to visit Nigeria.
On capacity building, the High Commissioner said India is ready to deepen its programme in Nigeria, noting that over 250 Nigerians benefit from the scheme every year.
He described Nigeria as a great country, stating that India holds Nigeria in high regard and that his country would be glad to receive the Minister.

title: ZAWYA: FG moves to deepen Nigeria, India bilateral ties in aviation
